title: Access-log search over the local chain while the central ledger is P7's
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 1, 11, 12.7, 19; RWB-P4-AD007-CON sections 11, 12.7
description: The access-log search answers from the local decision-record chain of rwb_access, while the central ledger is P7's decision_log_entry in rwb_decision. The sources do not say whether the audit search must span the whole ledger or only the entries the local chain holds.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-008 purpose 'Search the access log' with no join to rwb_decision; Architecture v5 slide 28 (each service writes its record in its own schema, rwb-decision collects it within 5 minutes) and slide 41 (P4 owns the access log, P7 owns the central ledger).
proposed: Build the search over the local chain of rwb_access and state on every answer the chain and the period it covers; give the end-to-end ledger view to the integration story.

title: The export file format, columns and row cap are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-007); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 12.1, 14; RWB-P4-AD007-CON sections 7 (AC3), 11, 12.1
description: The legacy story exports the search result with the same masking as the screen and names neither the media type, nor the column set and order, nor a row cap, nor the message of an over-cap answer.
evidence: RWB-AD-007 AC2 and test case TC-AD-007-02 name the export only; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-008 declares the search and no export operation.
proposed: Fix text/csv in UTF-8 with one header row, the thirteen columns decided_at to incident_reference in the order of the contract, the same masking as the screen, a cap of 10,000 rows and 422 above it, with the over-cap message left to the contract review.

title: No rule says which masking version applies to an old entry in the export
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 8 (BR8), 11; RWB-P4-AD007-CON section 15
description: An entry records the masking version it was written under, and masking_rule is versioned by valid_from and valid_to, but the sources do not say whether an export masks an old entry under the version recorded on it or under the version in force at export time.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 (masking_version, valid_from, valid_to); FSD P4 v3 A2.7 (the actions list the field IDs returned, marked masked) and A2.16 with no rule on a historical version.
proposed: The masking version recorded on the entry applies and is shown in its masking_version column, in the answer and in the file.

title: Whether a person may be searched by name is not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-007); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 8 (BR3), 11; RWB-P4-AD007-CON section 17
description: The legacy story says the log is searched by person while the target entry carries a user reference, and the sources do not say whether a name filter is accepted or a name is displayed.
evidence: RWB-AD-007 story text 'searched by person, date, event and capability area'; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-008 query parameter 'user' with no name field; NFR-040 data minimisation.
proposed: The search takes a staff user reference only; no name is accepted, displayed or logged, and no personal field leaves the service.

title: The retention of access entries is not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 3, 17, 19; RWB-P4-AD007-CON sections 13, 19
description: The access entry is a decision-record entry of the local chain, and the sources give no retention period or deletion rule for the access entries themselves.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28 (hash-linked local record, daily seal in write-only storage) with no retention period; TSD P4 v3 T7 with NFR-042 on logging and no access-log retention row.
proposed: Retention follows the decision log's retention rule (NFR-030); no separate rule is built for the access log.

title: rwb-access access review list: the review-cycle store is not defined in any source
source: Legacy RWB-AD-008 sections Data, Endpoints and Acceptance criteria; Arch v5 slide 41 P4 (rwb_access: Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.13 and A2.30
section: Section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.7 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Solution plan; section 15 Screens and states
description: The recertification needs a store for the review cycle and for one item per holder per role, and no source defines it. TSD P4 T3.1 lists role, permission, delegation_limit, lov_value, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case, masking_rule, role_conflict and partner_user, and has no access review object; the legacy story's Data table names assignment, decision_log_entry and role only. The field IDs, the column types, the unique keys and the state check are therefore this story's decision and the LDM and data dictionary have no rows for them.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 contains no access review object; FSD P4 v3 A2.13 and A2.30 define no review entity; Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the access log but no review store; Legacy RWB-AD-008 Data table lists assignment, decision_log_entry and role
owner_role: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead
proposed: Add access_review (review id, cycle code, opened_on, closes_on, state) and access_review_item (review, role code, holder reference, decision state, decision, reason, decided_at, decided_by reference, removal request reference) to the LDM, the data dictionary and the physical schema of rwb_access, allocate their field IDs at the next dictionary version, and carry them in RWB-P4-AD008-APP's migration.

title: rwb-access access review list: JOB-18 is a Temporal Schedule but the story metadata carries no workflow-kit dependency and no cron
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (TMP: Schedule access review list six-monthly) and slide 44 (JOB-18); Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet (JOB-18); Decision Log v10 DL38; story metadata of RWB-P4-AD008-APP
section: Metadata Depends on (build) and Patterns applied; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.5 and 12.6 Contract; section 13 Solution plan and Feature switch
description: Two values are missing. (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44 make the six-monthly access review list a Temporal Schedule of rwb-access, and DP-10 carries JOB-nn with the workflow kit RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, but the story's Depends on (build) list carries only RWB-P4-AD008-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, so the kit that creates the Schedule, runs AccessReviewWorkflow and runs the two activities is absent from the build order and from the pattern row. (2) The month, day and hour of the cron are stated nowhere; DL38 rules only the six-month placeholder until SCB IT security supplies the bank IAM standard value.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access exactly one Schedule, the six-monthly access review list, and slide 44 gives JOB-18 to rwb-access as a Schedule; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 records JOB-18 with Dependency None and failure action Rerun; DP-10 of Template and Rules R5.5 requires H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; the metadata of RWB-P4-AD008-APP lists no such dependency and its Patterns applied row is DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19
owner_role: Solution architect and the platform workflow owner
proposed: Add RWB-PLT-E1071-CON to the build list and DP-10 to the pattern row of RWB-P4-AD008-APP, fix the cron as deployment configuration of the access-review Schedule under the DL38 placeholder until the bank IAM standard value is supplied, and create the Schedule in the operations story of this legacy key.

title: rwb-access access review list: the bank IAM removal API is not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T5.1 (INT-21); TSD P2 Integration v3 (INT-21); Arch v5 slide 14 and 41 (REST ACE Common: sign-in, group-to-role); Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2
section: Section 4 Flow step 16 and 17; section 5 Exception paths X11; section 12.2 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Build steps
description: The close has to request the removal of every unconfirmed holder through the bank IAM, and no source gives that call a path, a request shape, an answer, a request reference or a failure contract. INT-21 names only the ACE sign-in and the group-to-role mapping at each sign-in, so the removal request, its acknowledgement and its refusal are a read, not a source value; the legacy story says only that the system requests removal through the bank IAM and logs it.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T5.1 row INT-21 Entra ID and the bank IAM, In, ACE sign-in, At each sign-in; TSD P2 v3 records the same row; Arch v5 slides 14 and 41 name only sign-in and group-to-role; Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2 Then the system requests removal through the bank IAM and logged
area: rwb-access integration with ACE Common and the bank IAM
owner_role: Solution architect and the ACE team integration owner
proposed: Fix the ACE Common group membership removal path in the integration catalogue and the P4 contract: the request (group, role code, holder reference, review and reason), the answer (request reference and accepted or refused), the INT-21 reference and the failure contract that leaves the item open with a task and an incident.

title: rwb-access access review list: the sources do not name the role owner who certifies a role
source: Legacy RWB-AD-008 Story line and Permission checks; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.13 and A2.30 roles and permissions tables
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 8; section 8 Business rules BR4; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract
description: The legacy story gives the list to each role owner and the permission check gives Platform administration R to RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM and RW-SECADM, but no source says which of them owns a role and may therefore confirm or remove its holders. TSD P4 T6.1 gives RW-SECADM CRUDA and RW-PLATADM CRUD in Platform administration, while RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY and RW-DATASTEW hold R only, so the ownership rule cannot be read off the matrix for the reference-data roles, and a caller with R only must not see a holder list.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-008 Story line As a role owner and Permission checks table (Platform administration R for six roles); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 rows RW-COE R, RW-DATASTEW R, RW-AUDIT R, RW-COMPLY R, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-SECADM CRUDA in Platform administration; FSD P4 v3 A2.30 roles table names the security administrator as primary
owner_role: Security administrator and the solution architect
proposed: Record in the access model and the PRD that the owner of a role is the holder of the A letter in Platform administration for that role (RW-SECADM and RW-PLATADM per TSD P4 T6.1), with RW-COE for the reference-data roles, and that a caller with R only owns no role and is refused.

title: rwb-access access review list: the state not confirmed is not defined
source: Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2; Decision Log v10 DL38 (leaver within the same working day); Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-18
section: Section 4 Flow step 16; section 8 Business rules BR8; section 9 State transitions; section 12.6 Schedules
description: Legacy AC2 acts on a holder not confirmed by the end of the review but no source says what makes an item not confirmed: whether an item with no decision is not confirmed, whether a role owner may leave an item undecided, or whether a rejection of the confirmation counts. The close therefore has no stated trigger for the removal request beyond the absence of a decision, and the leaver interval of DL38 is the only timing value in force.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2 Given a holder not confirmed by the end of the review; no state list for a review item in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 or T4; DL38 rules placeholder values for the review interval and the leaver response time only
proposed: State in the access model, the PRD and the screen text that an item with no decision at the close is not confirmed and triggers the removal request, and that the removal is requested within the DL38 leaver interval of the same working day.

title: List-of-values rows and reference-load endpoints are P3's while the console load is P4's
source: Ownership Map v1 (tables lov_value, reference_version, reference_row; api GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, POST /admin/reference-loads and its approve, verify and rollback); TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 API-P4-004 to API-P4-010; FSD P4 v3 A2.17; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
description: The R-PREC default ruling puts reference data and its operations with P3 rwb-case, and the TSD P4 v3 puts lov_value and the reference-load paths in the access module. The sources do not say which public path the Workbench console uses for a list-of-values load, so the boundary between the console ingest and the owner operation is undecided.
evidence: ownership.json: lov_value, reference_version and reference_row owner P3 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-5; GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, POST /admin/reference-loads, .../approve, .../verify and .../rollback owner P3 with ruling ASM-A6-api-4; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 carries API-P4-004 to API-P4-010 in the access module; no source names a console path for the load
proposed: rwb-access serves the console ingest and its checks under /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/lov-loads and calls the rwb-case reference-load contract; the two paths and the field name (table vs lovCode) are reconciled at contract review before the endpoint is frozen

title: The list-of-values load file format is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-009 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 lov_value DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033; FSD P4 v3 A2.17 (no load section)
description: The legacy story says only that a file is loaded for LOV-ROUTE, and the FSD module file has no section for a list-of-values load, so the file type, the header row and the column set are not specified.
evidence: Administration Stories v3 RWB-AD-009 AC1 'Given a file for LOV-ROUTE with codes and English labels'; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives the seven lov_value columns but no file format; FSD P4 v3 A2.17.3.2 field catalog covers role and permission only
proposed: CSV or XLSX with a header row and the columns value_code, label_en, label_th, sort_order and valid_from, matching TSD lov_value

title: The source and scope of the count of records using a value code are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-009 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T4; FSD P4 v3 A2.17
description: Legacy AC2 refuses a load that removes a code used by open cases with the count of records using the code, but no source says which records are counted, where the count is computed, or how it is worded on the screen.
evidence: Administration Stories v3 RWB-AD-009 AC2 'refuses it with the count of records using the code'; no FSD or TSD row defines the usage count; the ownership map gives the case to P3 and the list rows to P3
proposed: The count comes from the owner's reference-data usage check over the stored rows and the open cases and is returned in the 409 body as count beside valueCode; it is never recomputed in rwb-access and never names a case

title: The load checks other than the English label are not specified, and the FSD has no load section
source: Legacy RWB-AD-009 AC1 and AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.17 and FEAT-ADM-01; TSD P4 v3 T4
description: The FSD module file describes the administration screens as a whole and has no section for a list-of-values load, so the checks that a load runs, the order in which they run, and the way a failing row is named are not specified beyond the required English label and the code-in-use rule.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.17 has one success flow and two exception flows (role without the right, decision not recorded) and its field catalog is the role and permission screen; TSD P4 v3 T4 gives the version lifecycle only; no VR row covers the load
proposed: The checks are parse, required columns, required English label, duplicate value code in the file and against the list in force, unknown list code and valid-from present, with the Thai label optional; a failure is 422 naming the field and the row

title: The file-size and row caps of a load are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-009; TSD P4 v3 T7; FSD P4 v3 A2.17
description: No source gives a maximum file size or a maximum row count for a reference-data load, and no source says whether the caps are parameters or constants.
evidence: Administration Stories v3 RWB-AD-009 names no limit; TSD P4 v3 T7 lists no load limit; the FSD field catalog has no cap field
proposed: The caps are parameter rows read through DP-06: 5 MB and 5,000 rows, answered with 422 above either; the parameter keys are fixed at contract review

title: The reference-load approve path is P3's while the approval gate is P4's
source: Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve, verify and rollback (owner P3, ASM-A6-api-4); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A API-P4-006 (Reference data A); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 and 41
section: 1 Story; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The legacy story approved a reference load on one path, /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve, which TSD P4 appendix T-A gives to P4 with right A. The ownership map rules that path P3 rwb-case's under ASM-A6-api-4, because the version store (lov_value, reference_version, reference_row) is rwb-case's under ASM-A6-tables-5, while this story is P4's approval gate. No source says which path the administration console calls, or whether the console keeps a path of its own at all.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 (api.block for POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve: owner P3, ruling, asm ASM-A6-api-4); Ownership Map v1 tables lov_value, reference_version, reference_row (owner P3, ASM-A6-tables-5); TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 API-P4-006 and T-A.2; legacy RWB-AD-010 Endpoints table
proposed: Keep the gate and its authority with P4 as two console operations under /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/lov-loads, keep the version transition with rwb-case and call it as a consumed contract, and reconcile the two paths at contract review before either is frozen

title: The legacy permission row gives Reference data A to service identities while the legacy criterion has a person approving
source: Legacy RWB-AD-010 Permission checks table (Reference data A: Service identities only) and AC1; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix; FSD P4 v3 A2.17 roles
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules BR1; 10 Authority; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story's permission table says the A right in Reference data is held by service identities only, and its first acceptance criterion has a person, the list owner, approving a load. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-REFADM CRUD and RW-COE CRUD on Reference data and gives no person A, so neither the legacy row nor the TSD matrix as written supports a person approving.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-010 Permission checks table; Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-REFADM Reference data CRUD; RW-COE CRUD; SY-DATALOAD Reference data R); FSD P4 v3 A2.17.3.3 roles and permissions
proposed: Treat the TSD matrix as the source and the legacy row as the row under correction: the list owner holds A in Reference data through RW-REFADM and RW-COE, a service identity may author a load but not approve it, and the legacy permission row is corrected in the change register

title: An approval given before the valid-from date is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T4 state machine; FSD P4 v3 A2.22; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 note
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4; 8 Business rules BR5; 9 State transitions
description: The legacy criterion says an approved version takes effect from its valid-from date. No source says what happens when the approval is given before that date: whether the approval is refused until the date, whether the version sits in APPROVED until the date, or whether it goes straight to IN_FORCE. TSD T4 lists APPROVED and IN_FORCE as separate states but gives no rule for the gap, and the Drools design only states the approve-and-date discipline.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T4 (LOADED, APPROVED by a second person, IN_FORCE from its valid-from date); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 note (delegation limits follow the same approve-and-date discipline as the Drools packages); R-UNI-38
proposed: A version takes effect from its valid_from date only and never retroactively; an approval given before that date is allowed, the version reads APPROVED until the date and IN_FORCE from it, and the version it supersedes keeps valid_to set to the day before

title: How the four-eyes rule treats a service-identity author is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T4 and T6.3 author and approver; FSD P4 v3 A2.17 and A2.22
section: 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths X11; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2; 10 Authority
description: The legacy criterion refuses an approval by the person who loaded the version. Reference loads may also be authored by a service identity (the data load path SY-DATALOAD and the RW-REFADM load file), and no source says whether a service identity may approve, or whether a person may approve a load a service identity wrote.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T4 (APPROVED by a second person); TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (the author who loaded the version and the approver who approved it; the author cannot approve); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-REFADM prepares the load file; SY-DATALOAD Reference data R)
proposed: Compare the author reference with the approver reference; a service identity may not approve, and a person may approve a load a service identity wrote, with both references recorded in the decision-record entry

title: The refused self-approval uses MSG-P7-002, a decision-centre message
source: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC2 and Validation and messages table; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 v9 message catalogue (MSG-P7-002); TSD P4 v3 T6.3
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC2; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy criterion refuses the maker's approval with MSG-P7-002, which is the decision centre's message for an approver who prepared a decision. The P4 message list of the legacy story does not carry MSG-P7-002, so the criterion cites a message outside its own module's catalogue and no source says whether the reference-data refusal should reuse it or take a P4 id.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-010 AC2 and Validation and messages table (MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-003); User Stories Epic 1 v9 message table (MSG-P7-002, approver is the author: You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it.); TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (author and approver, MSG-P7-002)
proposed: Keep MSG-P7-002 word for word, as the legacy criterion writes it, and add it to the P4 message catalogue rather than renumbering the refusal, so one separation-of-duty rule keeps one message id in both places

title: rwb-access rule-version load: the rule registry is P7's but the story's contract-dependency list carries no P7 rule-package contract
source: Ownership Map v1 (tables rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case = P7, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3; api POST/GET /admin/rule-packages = P7, ruling ASM-A6-api-3); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.18 and FEAT-ADM-02; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-014, API-P4-015, API-P4-016; WP B-P4-03 metadata for RWB-P4-AD011-APP
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1 and 12.2 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Solution plan
description: The registry half of the legacy journey - the compile, the checks, the scenario run, the version states, the approval, the 00:01 promotion and the rollback - is rwb-decision's (P7) under the R-PREC default ruling, and the ownership map puts the rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case tables and the four rule-package paths there. The metadata of RWB-P4-AD011-APP carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON as a contract dependency, so the two rwb-decision operations the ingest and the read call have no published contract and no fake in the dependency list. The FSD A2.18 also presents the change as one journey in the P4 administration screens, which is the split this story records.
evidence: Ownership map ruling on rule_package: 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision (R-PREC default ruling; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slide 15)'; same ruling on rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case; api ruling on POST /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions: '... so the owner is P7' (ASM-A6-api-3); Architecture v5 slide 27 notes: 'Governance stays central in rwb-decision'; FSD P4 v3 A2.18.2 step 1 has the center of excellence analyst acting on the administration screen for the whole change; WP B-P4-03 story JSON for RWB-P4-AD011-APP lists C = [RWB-P3-E1042-CON] only.
proposed: Build the ingest and the read against the P7 rule-package contract and its fake, publish that contract with the P7 contract story of the legacy key, and add the missing C dependency RWB-P7-AD011-CON (or the id the P7 split allocates) to the metadata at D1.

title: rwb-access rule-version load: the compile, the checks and the SIT scenario run need the Drools kit RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, which is not in this story's build list
source: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 and notes; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-015 (compile, checks, scenarios) and T4; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04; WP B-P4-03 metadata for RWB-P4-AD011-APP (patterns DP05, DP06, DP13, DP19; H list without E1072)
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rules BR4; section 13 Solution plan and Pattern application
description: Legacy RWB-AD-011 AC1 says the rule table tests run in SIT and the result is attached to the version, and API-P4-015 puts the compile, the checks and the scenario run in the service that takes the upload. Compiling a Drools XLS decision table to DRL and running scenarios needs the embedded Drools kit, which DP-04 names as H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON. The ownership ruling moves the registry to P7 rwb-decision, and this story's pattern set deliberately omits DP-04, so the kit is neither a dependency here nor installed here; the story must therefore get the result from the registry and must not claim an evaluator of its own.
evidence: Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes: 'On upload the workbook is compiled to a KieBase, checked and run against at least 50 scenarios (rules.testcases.min=50), then stored as a rule_package_version row'; slide 15: governance is central in rwb-decision, evaluation is local in the owning service; DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; the story's H list is RWB-P4-AD011-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
area: rwb-access build dependency set and rule evaluation
proposed: Keep the compile, the checks and the SIT scenario run in rwb-decision where the kit lives, pass the workbook and show the returned result, and record in the build plan that rwb-access embeds no Drools kit and carries no DP-04.

title: rwb-access rule-version load: the route-set workbook format (sheet, header order, required columns) is not specified in any source
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 rule_row DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 and DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054, DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298, T-A.2 API-P4-015; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15; Legacy RWB-AD-011 data row rule_row; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.18
section: Section 1 Story; section 8 Business rules BR3; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Build steps 1 and 2
description: The sources name an Excel workbook in Drools XLS decision-table format and list the rule_row fields the parsed row must produce, but no source states the sheet name, the header row, the column order or which of the rule_row fields are mandatory in the upload. The app story needs that shape twice: to read the sheet before it forwards it, and to name the missing column in a 422.
evidence: TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-015 request: 'Multipart: file (xlsx), validFrom' with the purpose 'Upload an Excel workbook in Drools decision-table format'; T3.1 lists rule_row DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 plus DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054 and DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298 with no upload format; slide 15 only says 'RW-COE edits the Excel decision table'; legacy RWB-AD-011 data row lists rule_row fields DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 with no file shape.
proposed: Declare the workbook as the Drools XLS decision table carrying the rule_row columns plus test_case_id on every row, fix the sheet name and header order with the P7 registry owner and the center of excellence, and add them to the rwb-access contract before the parser is frozen.

title: rwb-access rule-version load: what the result attached to the version means is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-AD-011 AC1; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 DF-REF-292 and DF-REF-293, T6.3; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.18.4.1 AC-P4-018-01
section: Section 1 Story; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; section 8 Business rules BR8; section 11 Data; section 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy criterion says the rule table tests run in SIT and 'the result is attached to the version', without saying what the attached result is made of, where it is stored or how a reader sees it. The technical specification holds test_result (DF-REF-292) and dry_run_counts (DF-REF-293) on the package version, and FSD AC-P4-018-01 says only that the result is recorded with its rule version.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-011 AC1: 'Then the rule table tests run in SIT and the result is attached to the version'; TSD P4 T3.1 rule_package_version has DF-REF-292 test_result (LOV-TEST-RESULT) and DF-REF-293 dry_run_counts (jsonb); TSD P4 T6.3 records the checksum, the author and approver and the decision log linkage but no SIT report field; FSD P4 A2.18.4.1: 'The result is recorded with its rule version'.
proposed: Read the attached result as the registry's test_result and dry_run_counts of the package version, returned by the load and shown with the SIT report reference the registry returns; confirm the SIT report reference with the registry owner and add it to the contract.

title: rwb-access rule-version load: whether a row without a test case ID refuses the version at upload or at approval is ambiguous
source: Legacy RWB-AD-011 AC2; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-015 (errors 409 and 422) and API-P4-017 (approval refused while the checklist is incomplete); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 (load checks); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.18.4
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow step 9; section 5 Exception paths X4; section 8 Business rules BR1 and BR2
description: The legacy criterion says a row with no test case ID makes the system refuse the version, but not at which step: the upload could refuse it (422 against the file) or the registry could load it and the approval could refuse it with the change checklist. The technical specification puts a failed load at REFUSED and the approval behind a checklist, so both readings are supported by the sources, and the difference decides whether a bad workbook is stored at all.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-011 AC2: 'Given a row with no test case ID / When I load it / Then the system refuses the version'; TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-015 errors include 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 and API-P4-017 refuses an approval while a change_checklist item is missing; TSD P4 T4: 'A load that fails any check is REFUSED and is never in force'; slide 15 load checks are compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, at least 50 scenarios, dry run, and none of them is the test case ID.
proposed: Refuse at upload, with the row number and the field name, before the registry is called and before any version is stored, and keep the registry's own checks as the second gate on its side.
